If the _vex function does not exist, it will cause an error.

String replacement may incorrectly replace the _vex() string within the function body.

Suggested improvements:

```
# Check if base completion exists
if declare -f _vex >/dev/null 2>&1; then

    eval "$(declare -f _vex | sed '1s/_vex/_vex_base/')"
else
    # Fallback: define empty base function
    _vex_base() { :; }

```

The _vex_get_configs() function does not handle command failure scenarios. If vex list fails, it will return an empty list, leaving users unaware of what went wrong. The failure of any command in the pipeline may lead to unexpected results. It is recommended to improve it as follows:

```
_vex_get_configs() {
    local output
    output=$({bin_name} list 2>/dev/null)
    if [ $? -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$output" ]; then
        echo "$output" | grep ' - ' | awk '{{print $1}}'
    fi
}
```

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match zsh subcommands from parsed argument state**

In the zsh completion function, the `args` branch now switches on `words[1]`, but this array element is the command token in completion context, not the parsed subcommand selected by `_arguments`. As a result, the `exec|rm|edit|rename` arms do not trigger and dynamic config-name completion is skipped for those subcommands. Using the parsed positional value (`line[1]`) preserves the intended behavior.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop escaping env substitutions passed to Command::args**

`exec_command` executes QEMU with `Command::new(...).args(&exec_args)`, so the arguments are passed directly to the child process rather than interpreted by a shell. Escaping `${VAR}` replacements here therefore injects literal backslashes into real argument values (for example, `#`, `$`, `*`, `?`), which can break valid paths/options and make previously working configs fail whenever those characters appear in environment variables.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Create rc-file parent directories before opening**

`init_command` opens the target rc/profile file directly, but several supported shells use nested paths (for example `~/.config/fish/config.fish` and `~/.config/powershell/...`) whose parent directories may not exist on first-time setups. In that case `vex init --shell fish`/`powershell` fails with `ENOENT` instead of completing installation, so this path should ensure `rc_file.parent()` is created before `open`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle quoted $EDITOR values correctly**

Using `split_whitespace()` to parse `EDITOR` breaks valid editor commands that rely on quoting (for example, paths with spaces on Windows/macOS), so `Command::new` receives a truncated program token and `vex edit` fails to launch the editor. This is user-visible for common setups like `"C:\Program Files\..." --wait`, so the editor command should be parsed with shell-quoting semantics instead of plain whitespace splitting.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid auto-running VMs when edit runs without stdin**

This prompt path calls `prompt_user()` for a `Y/n` confirmation, but that helper treats empty input (including EOF) as `true`; in non-interactive runs (stdin closed/piped), editing any config change will therefore execute `exec_command` without explicit consent. That can unexpectedly start QEMU in scripts/CI, so this branch should default to "no" when input is non-interactive or unavailable.

In `clone_remote_repo`, `git clone` is executed with `current_dir` set to a temporary directory, so a relative `VEX_REMOTE_URL` is interpreted relative to that temp path instead of the user's working directory. This breaks the documented "local repository path" workflow for common inputs like `VEX_REMOTE_URL=../remote.git`, which will fail with "repository does not exist" unless users provide an absolute path.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Let Ctrl+C quit from help overlay**

When the help overlay is visible, this early return converts every key press, including Ctrl+C, into `DismissHelp`, so the documented "Ctrl+C force quit" behavior and the later "Ctrl+C is always Quit" branch are bypassed. In a stuck or misbehaving TUI state with help open, users have to press Ctrl+C twice rather than getting the expected immediate quit; handle the Ctrl+C check before the help-overlay swallow path.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep right-pane scroll state at the real bottom**

When focus is on the right pane, pressing `G` stores `u16::MAX`; `render_cards_area` only clamps that value locally for drawing and explicitly never writes it back, so subsequent Up events subtract from 65535 and the view remains pinned to the bottom for tens of thousands of keypresses. This makes normal scroll-back unusable after jumping to the bottom of any details pane; store the actual max scroll or clamp the state before applying `NavigateUp`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp the help popup to the terminal size**

When the terminal is narrower than 40 columns or shorter than 12 rows, `clamp(40, 64)` / `clamp(12, 24)` expands the popup rectangle beyond the frame. Rendering `Clear` and the `Paragraph` with that out-of-buffer `Rect` can panic in Ratatui, so pressing `?` after starting or resizing to a small terminal exits the TUI instead of just drawing a smaller help box.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Hide details when the active filter has no matches**

With a non-empty config set and a filter that matches nothing, `app.is_empty()` is still false, so the UI renders both panes; the left pane has no selected row, but the right pane displays `app.entries[app.selected]` (usually the first hidden config). This makes a zero-result filter show details for a configuration that is not visible/selectable, so the empty/no-match state should be based on `visible_indices()` or the right pane should be suppressed when there is no visible selection.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Write renamed config before removing original file**

In rename-on-save (`EditMode::Update`), the old config file is deleted before the new file is written. If the subsequent write fails (for example due to permissions, quota, or disk-full errors), the user loses both the original and renamed config. Save should be made failure-atomic by writing/replacing the new file first and only then removing the old path.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve builtin-name overrides when saving snippet edits**

This rebuilds the persisted user-snippet list by dropping every merged entry whose name matches a builtin. That silently discards existing user overrides that intentionally reuse builtin names (the merge contract supports override-by-name), so a normal snippet edit can erase unrelated overrides from `snippets.json`. Persisted entries should be filtered by source/origin, not by name equality with builtins.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid dropping builtin-name overrides during delete flow**

The delete-confirm path recomputes `user_only` by excluding all snippets whose names match builtins, so confirming deletion of one snippet can also remove unrelated user overrides of builtin names from disk. This causes unexpected data loss for valid user libraries that rely on override-by-name behavior.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Commit active arg-token edit before Ctrl+S save**

When an Edit session is in Args token-edit mode, `Ctrl+S` is handled by the common shortcut branch before the token-edit branch runs, so `EditSave` persists `edit.args` without applying the in-progress `token_edit` buffer. This silently drops the user's latest token changes if they save directly from token-edit mode; save should first commit the token (or be blocked until commit).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Save snippets in documented default location**

This path is derived from `config_dir()` and becomes `<default config dir>/snippets.json`; with the current default config dir (`~/.vex/configs`), snippets are written to `~/.vex/configs/snippets.json` rather than `~/.vex/snippets.json` as documented in this release notes/README and rendered in the library UI. Users expecting the advertised file location will see their existing snippet library ignored.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow library saves that override builtin snippet names**

The merge contract in this feature is name-based override, but this guard rejects any snippet whose name matches a builtin, making builtin overrides impossible to create/update from Library mode. That prevents users from performing the advertised override workflow through the UI and forces manual file edits for a core use case.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat overridden builtin snippets as user-editable**

This gate classifies snippets as builtin purely by name, which breaks the documented override flow: users can create a snippet with a builtin name (e.g. `Cortex-A72`) and it correctly persists as a user override, but selecting that merged row later is blocked as “builtin” for edit/delete. In practice, any user override whose name collides with a builtin becomes unmanageable from Library mode, even though it is stored in `user_only` and expected to be user-owned.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow snippet names beyond config-name charset**

Do not validate library snippet names with `validate_config_name`, because that rule rejects spaces and most punctuation while builtin snippet names include spaces (e.g., `"1G memory"`, `"no graphics"`). In Library mode this prevents creating or saving overrides for most builtins by name, so the advertised “user overrides builtin by name” flow fails for nearly all builtin entries unless users edit JSON manually.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Classify snippet source from persisted user overrides**

The detail/source classification is currently based only on whether the name exists in the builtin list, so a user override that intentionally collides with a builtin name is rendered as `builtin (read-only)` even though it is actually editable/deletable as a user entry. This creates contradictory UI state in Library mode and can mislead users away from editing the existing override.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reselect after edit save when a filter is active**

When a config is saved from Edit mode, the rescan path always sets `selected` to the saved entry by name, but it never re-applies filter visibility. In `BrowseSubMode::Filtering { accepted: true, .. }`, renaming an entry so it no longer matches the active query leaves selection pointing at a hidden row: the left list shows no selected item while the right pane still renders that hidden config, and follow-up actions (like launch) can fail with "not visible" errors. This save path should call the same filtered reselect logic used by refresh.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Drop empty args before persisting edited configurations**

Edit mode can create empty arg tokens (`EditArgsAddEmpty` inserts `""`), and `EditSave` commits that token even if the user never typed content. This save path then writes `edit.args` verbatim, so empty strings are persisted into config JSON and later passed to `Command`, which can break VM launches or produce confusing runtime errors. Snippet-save already strips empty args, so config-save should apply equivalent sanitization before writing.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use replace-safe file swap for snippets.json writes**

`save_user_snippets` writes to a temp file and then calls `std::fs::rename(tmp, path)`; this is platform-dependent when the destination already exists, so on some Windows/filesystem combinations the rename can fail instead of replacing the old file. After the first successful save creates `snippets.json`, later snippet create/edit/delete operations can start failing at this step even though the new JSON was prepared correctly.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep library write operations read-only after load errors**

When entering Library mode, `load_user_snippets()` errors are silently converted to an empty `user_only` baseline via `unwrap_or_default()`. If the existing `snippets.json` is temporarily unreadable or malformed, any subsequent save/delete in Library mode rewrites disk from that empty baseline, which can wipe previously stored user snippets instead of forcing the user to resolve the load error first.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid hardcoding CLI version in integration test**

The `--version` test currently asserts a fixed string (`0.4.0`), so any normal crate version bump will fail CI even when CLI behavior is still correct. This creates a recurring false-negative test failure on every release/version update. Use the package version at build time (for example via `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`) so the test validates behavior instead of pinning one specific release number.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

-
